title: Regional inference interruption — customer briefing (draft)
summary: Draft set of customer-facing communications and status page snippets describing the January 27 regional inference interruption affecting EU-West. Includes suggested status page timeline updates, a concise postmortem for customers, impact metrics, and recommended customer actions.
content:
Overview:
On 2026-01-27 08:12 UTC we detected elevated latencies and an increase in 5xx errors for inference requests routed through the EU-West region. The degradation persisted intermittently for ~3 hours and caused increased tail latency for a subset of customers using the hosted API. This draft provides short status page copy for progressive updates, and a customer-facing postmortem summary.

Scope & impact (customer-facing summary):
- Affected region: EU-West (primary routing for customers in EU).
- Affected features: text generation and chat endpoints using the standard hosted models. Embeddings and dedicated infra customers were largely unaffected.
- User impact: increased request latency (median latency rose from ~120ms to ~350ms, p99s up to 2.6s) and a spike in transient 502/504 errors for ~6% of requests during the peak window.
- Duration: intermittent between 2026-01-27 08:12 UTC and 2026-01-27 11:35 UTC. Full return to nominal behavior confirmed by 11:45 UTC.

Suggested status page snippets (short form) — for posting in staggered updates:
1) Initial detect (08:20 UTC):
- Title: Elevated latency and transient errors in EU-West
- Body: We are investigating increased latency and transient errors for inference requests routed to EU-West. Some requests may return failures or experience higher latency. Engineers are actively investigating and routing adjustments are in progress. We will post updates every 30–60 minutes.

2) Mitigation in progress (09:05 UTC):
- Title: Partial traffic reroute and operational mitigations underway
- Body: We have applied a targeted routing policy to shift a portion of EU-West traffic to nearby regions and enabled a model-variant fallback to reduce load on impacted nodes. These steps have reduced error rates for most customers; we are continuing to monitor and stabilize tail latency.

3) Degraded but stabilizing (10:45 UTC):
- Title: Service stabilizing; monitoring continues
- Body: Error rates and latency are substantially reduced thanks to routing changes and autoscaler adjustments. Some requests may still see elevated latency while remaining mitigation work completes. No action needed from customers at this time.

4) Service restored (11:50 UTC):
- Title: Incident resolved — EU-West latency restored
- Body: The service is operating within normal parameters. We continue to monitor closely. A customer-facing postmortem is being prepared and will be published within 5 business days.

Customer-facing postmortem draft (concise):
- What happened: A regression introduced in a recent scheduler change caused uneven GPU slot allocation in EU-West. The regressed behavior, combined with a kernel-selection edge case for a specific model size, led to elevated memory pressure on several serving nodes. This caused increased request queuing and a higher rate of transient failures for a subset of routed requests.

- Why it impacted customers: The combination of scheduler allocation skew and the kernel-selection fallback path materially increased per-request processing time and reduced effective throughput on impacted hosts. Because EU-West had a higher proportion of bursty request patterns at the time of the regression, the local autoscaler reacted by cycling pods in a way that temporarily amplified the instability.

- Detection & response timeline (UTC):
  - 08:12: First alerts for elevated p99 latency and increased 5xx rates from synthetic canaries and customer telemetry.
  - 08:20: On-call SRE triaged; initial hypothesis pointed to runtime kernel degradation.
  - 08:45: Team confirmed allocation skew correlated with new scheduler code (release v2.14.1).
  - 09:05: Routing policy applied to shift 30% of EU-West traffic to EU-Central; model-variant fallback enabled.
  - 09:40: Autoscaler tuning and pod draining reduced error rates; tail latency still elevated.
  - 10:30: Hotfix deployed to rollback the scheduler change in EU-West.
  - 11:35: Error rates returned to baseline; gradual verification completed.
  - 11:45: Full monitoring signals green; post-incident verification started.

- Root cause (short technical explanation):
A scheduler regression changed the slot packing heuristic for colocated inference workers. Under a specific mix of request sequence lengths and model sizes, the runtime triggered an atypical kernel selector fallback that uses a slower execution path and higher host memory for temporary buffers. This created sustained memory pressure which increased I/O and CPU contention; the autoscaler then oscillated, causing higher error rates and amplified latencies.

- Actions we took (immediate):
1. Rolled back the scheduler change in EU-West (hotfix).
2. Applied targeted traffic reroutes to reduce load on impacted hosts.
3. Enabled model fallback variants to reduce kernel-selector invocation frequency.
4. Tuned autoscaler thresholds to avoid oscillation while stabilizing nodes.
5. Enhanced monitoring to include an allocation-imbalance alert and a kernel-fallback metric.

- Next steps (what we will do to prevent recurrence):
1. Revert the regression permanently after adding deterministic unit tests around slot packing heuristics and a regression test that simulates the bursty request mix (owner: infra/runtime).
2. Add a canary test that exercises the kernel-selection fallback under load before any runtime release (owner: serving-runtime).
3. Improve autoscaler hysteresis and add protection to avoid pod churn in the presence of allocation imbalance (owner: sre/platform).
4. Post-deployment: a 30-day telemetry review to verify no recurrence and to assess long-tail impact on customer request patterns.

Customer impact, credits, and suggested action: 
- Impact: Short-term increased latency and transient errors for a subset of requests in EU-West during the window described above. No customer data was exposed, modified, or lost.
- Credits: We will proactively apply a service credit covering one day of token usage pro-rated to customers who experienced increased error rates (implementation details to be communicated by account teams).
- Recommended customer action: No action required to resume normal service. If you rely on strict latency SLAs, we recommend pinning a dedicated route to a Redwood Dedicated pool or configuring a geo-preference in the routing settings; account teams can assist.

Notes for the comms owner (internal):
- Tone: Keep language clear, avoid excessive technical jargon, emphasize remediation and customer impact.
- FAQs to prepare: how credits are calculated; which customers will receive outreach; whether embeddings or dedicated customers were affected.
- Attachments for publishing: timeline graph (p99/p50/p95), error-rate chart by minute, list of affected customer IDs (internal), link to full technical postmortem for enterprise accounts.

Open items / TODOs: 
- [ ] Confirm credit calculation and finalize customer notification list (owner: CS ops)
- [ ] Produce final graph assets for status page and customer emails (owner: observability)
- [ ] Finalize wording and approvals from legal for external postmortem (owner: customer-success lead)

Draft sign-off lines (suggested):
- Short: "We’re sorry for the disruption. Our team has implemented a fix and we’re taking steps to reduce the likelihood of this happening again. For account-specific questions, contact your Customer Success Manager."
- Longer (for enterprise customers): "We understand the operational impact this incident had on your applications and are committed to continuous improvement. We will apply a pro-rated service credit and are available to discuss additional mitigations such as dedicated routing and regional failover guidance."

Appendix (brief internal technical notes for CS engineering):
- Key logs and traces: stack traces show increased allocations in the runtime kernel selection module under specific model-size requests.
- Hotfix details: rolled back commit sha: a3f9d2b. Deployed to EU-West only at 10:30 UTC, full rollback queued for other regions after validation.
- Monitoring added: metric runtime.kernel_fallback.count and infra.allocation_variance_ratio with alert thresholds.

End of draft.

Change log for this draft: 2026-01-28 initial draft by EMR; 2026-01-29 updated timeline/metrics from observability; 2026-02-02 added credit language and final sign-off lines for review.
